slides.title: Header File Guards Purpose
slides.prompt: Why do C++ header files use '#pragma once' or inclusion guards (#ifndef / #define)?
options: To prevent duplicate symbol definition errors during compilation
To speed up execution runtime performance
slides.correctAnswer: To prevent duplicate symbol definition errors during compilation

slides.title: Header Guard Preprocessor Directives

slides.title: One Definition Rule (ODR)
slides.prompt: According to the One Definition Rule (ODR), how many definitions can a non-inline function have across the entire program?
options: Exactly one definition across all translation units
One definition per header file included
Unlimited definitions as long as parameter names differ
slides.correctAnswer: Exactly one definition across all translation units

slides.title: Modern Pragmatic Header Guard
slides.prompt: Fill in the non-standard but widely supported modern single-line header guard directive.

slides.title: Parameter Names in Prototypes
slides.prompt: Are parameter names strictly required in function forward declarations/prototypes?
options: No, parameter types are mandatory, but names are optional
Yes, parameter names must match the definition exactly
Yes, parameter names are required by the C++ standard
No, neither types nor names are required
slides.correctAnswer: No, parameter types are mandatory, but names are optional

slides.title: Translation Units and Functions
slides.prompt: What happens when a declared function is called in main() but lacks any definition during compilation?
options: A Linker Error (e.g., unresolved external symbol)
slides.correctAnswer: A Linker Error (e.g., unresolved external symbol)
